evidence_weights.PARTIAL: real but limited (short history, gaps, snapshot only): weigh with the stated limitation
evidence_weights.RESEARCH: non-production or experimental: lower-confidence evidence; never the sole basis of a recommendation
evidence_weights.UNKNOWN: status not established: treat as context only
evidence_weights.VERIFIED: production-generated, tested, historically covered: weigh fully

forbidden: treating a model price or repository recommendation as a bet instruction
inventing injuries, lineups, weather, usage or prices absent from the packet
recommending a position without a fair probability and a bet-up-to price
outputs_required: evidence inventory with quality statuses and gaps
three or more game scripts with likelihoods
per-position: fair probability, bet-up-to price, confidence, strongest counter-case, correlation note
explicit PASS where no edge exists
explicit treatment of each user-focus item
principles: Projections, model prices and repository recommendations are EVIDENCE. They are never automatic bets and never authoritative.
Form at least three plausible game scripts before pricing anything; say which evidence supports each.
For every candidate position, state the strongest counter-case and the single most likely way it loses.
Prefer opponent-adjusted and schedule-adjusted information where the packet marks it VERIFIED; treat unadjusted values as context, not conclusions.
Inspect every market included in the packet before choosing an expression; the best expression of a view is often not the first market read.
Compare alternate expressions of the same view (full game vs period, spread vs moneyline vs total, team vs player) and explain the choice.
Distinguish independent edges from correlated positions; never count the same thesis twice.
Estimate your OWN fair probability for each position and show the reasoning; do not copy the model price.
Give a bet-up-to price (the highest price at which the position still carries a positive expected value under your fair probability).
PASS is a complete answer. When no compelling, independent, well-priced edge exists, say so.
RESEARCH-status data is lower-confidence evidence; say when a conclusion rests on it.
Never invent missing inputs. If the packet says a datum is missing or stale, reason with that gap explicitly.
Respect the price timestamps: a quote older than the packet's freshness threshold is a reference, not an executable price.
Bankroll, staking and placement are outside this protocol: output fair probabilities and bet-up-to prices only.
sport_notes: Minutes and usage are the first question for any player prop; a rotation change outweighs season averages.
Pace and rest (back-to-backs) move totals; treat preseason data as RESEARCH.
Live-season sample sizes are small early; prefer market-anchored priors until the sample grows.

steps.instruction: Restate the scope (game / slate / custom tray), the data as-of time and the freshness of markets and model evidence.
List the evidence by entity with its quality status (VERIFIED / PARTIAL / RESEARCH) and note what is missing.
Write three or more plausible game scripts with rough likelihoods that sum to about one; tie each to specific evidence.
Go through every market in the packet; for each family note the current YES bid/ask and the implied probability.
For the markets your scripts bear on, estimate an independent fair probability with a short derivation.
Compare your fair probability with the model evidence; explain agreements and disagreements rather than averaging blindly.
For each view, compare alternate expressions and pick the one with the best price-to-thesis fit; state correlation with other picks.
For each candidate position, write the strongest reason it loses and whether that risk is priced.
Output RECOMMEND / LEAN / PASS per position with fair probability, bet-up-to price, confidence, and the evidence status it rests on.
Address every item the user placed in the research tray explicitly, even when the verdict is PASS.
